summary: Regression test of Locat UI 3.0 (standalone Vite preview at http://localhost:5173) after react-hooks v7 refactor. Verified: app shell with 21 desktop sidebar items and 5 mobile bottom-tabs (tab-chats/tab-media/tab-home/tab-devices/tab-more); Ctrl+K command palette (input auto-focus, live filter, Esc close, fresh mount on reopen resets query); deep-link /devices?pair=1 via palette opens data-testid=pair-sheet and clears the URL param on close; /messages?compose=1 via direct URL opens data-testid=new-conversation-sheet; opening a conversation (conversation-c-mira) renders virtual list and keyboard roving focus works (End key); desktop context menu (data-testid=context-menu, 3+ ctx-* items) opens near right/bottom edge and stays inside viewport (clamping OK), ArrowDown + Esc close works; on mobile 390x844 the desktop context menu is NOT rendered and an ActionMenu sheet (role=dialog) appears instead; drop-overlay (data-testid=drop-overlay) appears on window dragenter with Files; Settings → Appearance theme switch works (obsidian → graphite reflected on documentElement[data-theme]); Component Gallery (/gallery) renders cleanly with Foundations/Actions/Inputs/Status/States/Lists/Overlays/Messaging tabs; module tour across home/cinema/music/photos/devices/remote/sentinel/vault/search/hub/offline/modules produced ZERO console errors. ESLint on src/**/*.{ts,tsx} is clean (0 warnings, 0 errors). One infra blocker was fixed: Vite dev server had a stale in-memory module graph still pointing to pre-refactor .tsx paths (/src/app/back.tsx, /src/app/session.tsx, /src/ui/Toast.tsx all 404 even though the files are now .ts); restarting the Vite process from /app/locat-ui-3.0 cleared this and the app renders cleanly. No source code was changed.

integration_issues.issue: Typing 'new conversation' in the palette does NOT match the compose action (its keywords are 'new chat message compose'), so pressing Enter does not navigate to /messages?compose=1. Direct URL navigation to /messages?compose=1 correctly opens the new-conversation-sheet, so the deep-link itself is intact; only the palette keyword list is incomplete. Suggest adding 'conversation' to the k-string of the new-chat action in /app/locat-ui-3.0/src/layouts/CommandPalette.tsx line 27.

action_items: Optional (minor): extend the compose action's keywords in src/layouts/CommandPalette.tsx so that typing 'new conversation' in Ctrl+K also opens /messages?compose=1 (currently only 'compose', 'chat', or 'message' match). All other deep-link flows are functioning.

Dev-ops: whenever source files are renamed .tsx↔.ts in /app/locat-ui-3.0, restart the Vite dev server (kill the running npx vite PIDs and relaunch `npx vite --host 0.0.0.0 --port 5173`); the stale module graph will otherwise serve 404s for the old extension forever. This is Vite-standard behaviour, not a code bug.
critical_code_review_comments: CommandPalette is correctly refactored to mount a fresh <Palette> only when `open` is true, so query/selection state is reset without an effect — matches the request. useEffect with 20ms timeout for input focus is clean, cleaned up on unmount.

ContextMenuProvider.CursorMenu uses useLayoutEffect to position via placeMenu(x, y, w, h, innerWidth, innerHeight) which correctly clamps the popover inside the viewport; verified with right-click at (vw-20, vh-20): popover's right/bottom stayed <= viewport. On widths <768 it falls back to <ActionMenu> sheet (role=dialog) — verified at 390 wide.

DropProvider uses stackRef (updated via useLayoutEffect) to read the latest target inside stable DOM listeners — no stale closures, no sync setState in effect. Overlay is portal-mounted with data-testid=drop-overlay.
Virtual.tsx keyboard handler is pure (uses focusIdx ref, no setState in render), scrollToIndex is memoized, Edge case: non-input targets only — correctly ignores keystrokes inside input/textarea.
ESLint under react-hooks v7 rules passes with zero errors/warnings; no Date.now() in render, no refs read during render, no sync setState in useEffect across the files of reference.

success_rate.frontend: ~95% (12/13 flows pass; palette-keyword gap on 'new conversation' is the only miss; deep link itself works via direct URL)

seed_data_creation: None. All data served by src/fixtures/previewAdapter.ts (c-mira, c-studio with largeLibraries=5000, FIXTURE_PHOTOS, etc.).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Vite dev server runs at http://localhost:5173 (NOT managed by supervisor — it's launched manually via `cd /app/locat-ui-3.0 && npx vite --host 0.0.0.0 --port 5173 &`). After any .tsx↔.ts rename on disk, kill all vite PIDs and relaunch to clear the stale module graph (symptom: 404s on /src/app/back.tsx, /src/app/session.tsx, /src/ui/Toast.tsx). Entry flow: welcome-signin → login-username/password (focus wrapper, then keyboard.type) → login-submit → continue-demo-button. Correct testIDs: `conversation-${id}` (NOT conv-${id}), `theme-${id}` (obsidian/graphite/daylight/system), `tab-chats|tab-media|tab-home|tab-devices|tab-more` on mobile, `nav-${id}` on desktop. Settings pages are at /settings/${id}; appearance exposes theme-* buttons. page.goto() resets session back to welcome because session state is in-memory only (by design) — use in-app clicks or re-enter via Entry flow after each goto.
rca_of_issue: During the first automation pass the app rendered a blank page and the browser console showed 404s on /src/app/back.tsx, /src/app/session.tsx, /src/ui/Toast.tsx. On disk those files exist only as .ts — a rename was done as part of the refactor. The already-running Vite dev process had cached the transformed /src/ui/index.ts re-exports with the old .tsx paths and the stale ?t= timestamps served from before the rename. curl /src/ui/index.ts confirmed `export * from "/src/ui/Toast.tsx"` (stale) was being served; after restarting vite the same URL served `export * from "/src/ui/Toast.ts"` (correct). No source change was required. Mitigation: either `touch /app/locat-ui-3.0/src/ui/index.ts` to invalidate the module in HMR, or kill+restart the vite PIDs. This is an environment artefact, not a bug in the Locat UI code.
